title: Account Balance After Rounded Purchase
summary: Starting with a bank balance of 100 dollars, you spend an amount represented by an integer purchaseAmount.
statement: Starting with a bank balance of 100 dollars, you spend an amount represented by an integer purchaseAmount. This amount is rounded to the nearest multiple of 10, and that rounded amount is deducted from your balance. Return the final balance, noting that 0 is a multiple of 10 and 5 rounds up.
constraints: Round purchaseAmount to the nearest multiple of ten; when equally close, round upward.
Begin with an account balance of one hundred.
Return the balance after subtracting the rounded purchase.
hints: Adding five before integer division implements nearest-ten rounding with upward ties.
Subtract that rounded value from one hundred.
The five-unit shift places every rounding boundary at an integer quotient boundary, including the specified tie direction.
editorial: The five-unit shift places every rounding boundary at an integer quotient boundary, including the specified tie direction.

tests.explanation: Nine rounds to ten, leaving ninety.
The tie between ten and twenty rounds upward to twenty, leaving eighty.
